title: Relocating family engages, then opts out mid-call
scenario: Mom relocating for her husband's job starts out friendly, gives details, then gets overwhelmed by other lenders' calls and asks to be removed. The rep honors it immediately.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: Hi, is this Shauna? It's Paolo with Copperleaf Home Loans.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Hi, yes. Oh gosh, another call. Sorry, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: No worries. You'd mentioned you're relocating and looking at buying?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Yeah, my husband's company is moving us to Raleigh in January. Two kids, a dog, the whole circus.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: That's a big move. Are you selling your current house?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: We're renting it out, actually. We want to keep it.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: Smart. And for the new place, are you thinking a similar price range?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Probably a little more. Things are pricier there. Maybe four-fifty?

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: Okay. And is your husband's employer offering any relocation assistance?

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: Some, I think. Honestly, I've had like nine lenders call me today. My phone hasn't stopped since I filled out that form.

utterances.speaker: client
utterances.text: It is. You know what, I'm sorry, but please just take me off your list. Don't call me again.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: Absolutely, I understand. I'll remove you from our call list right now.

utterances.speaker: rep
utterances.text: None taken at all. Good luck with the move, Shauna.
